clue.text: It provides for change of cast in play

definitions.text: It provides for change of cast in play

parts.words: It provides for change of cast in play
parts.note: read as theatre jargon, the cast of a play changes its costumes in this backstage room

explanation.surface: A theatre manager arranges for actors to be replaced mid-run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of cast' suggests swapping actors; it is the actors changing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstage room where actors put on and take off costumes between scenes fits the cryptic reading.

clue.text: Head of department went fishing and got suspended

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of department

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line, so went fishing means angled

explanation.surface: A department boss went fishing and was suspended from work for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got suspended' suggests a punishment at work; here it means hung loosely, like bait on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hung loosely or swung from a support was suspended, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: School training EU cadet

indicators.note: training puts the letters through drills that rearrange them into a new order

explanation.surface: A European military cadet is being schooled and drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or instruct them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Votes against keeping temperature records

indicators.note: keeping says one word holds another inside it, as if storing it

parts.note: noes are the votes cast against a motion

explanation.surface: Dissenting votes in a meeting are kept in the record along with the temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are written records of something, as in notes of a meeting, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Artist acknowledging applause for display of colour

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
a performer acknowledging applause is in a bow, bent forward to the audience

explanation.surface: A painter takes a bow for a vivid exhibition of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectral colours in the sky is nature's most familiar display of colour.

clue.text: Continually moving forward when leaving

definitions.meaning: describes something in progress and carrying on without a break
split into two words, it reads 'on departure', the moment of leaving

explanation.surface: Someone keeps advancing even as they head for the exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing means in progress and continuing; read as two words it means at the moment of departure.

clue.text: Last minute, though well before noon

definitions.meaning: the latest possible moment for something to be done
the hour numbered eleven on a clock comes a while before midday

explanation.surface: A deadline is reached at the last moment, yet it is still morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' joins the two senses: a phrase meaning last-minute names a time that is in fact an hour before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the last possible moment literally names the hour before twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Right out, made alluring slip of the tongue

indicators.note: a slip is a mistake that jumbles things, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out says this letter is to be taken away from the word

explanation.surface: A tempting remark turned into a Freudian slip of the tongue once 'right' was gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' takes R from alluring, leaving ALLUING, which 'slip' rearranges. 'Slip of the tongue' looks like one phrase but splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingual is an adjective meaning relating to the tongue, from the Latin word lingua.

clue.text: One so happy tends to act rashly

definitions.text: One so happy tends to act rashly

parts.words: One so happy tends to act rashly
parts.note: read as a firearm's lever followed by 'happy', the phrase describes someone quick to shoot

explanation.surface: A cheerful person is prone to impulsive behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry is only the first half of a hyphenated phrase: with 'happy' after it, it names a person who fires without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described with this word plus 'happy' is reckless and quick to shoot, so acts rashly.

clue.text: Using ruler, check a line for capital waterway

parts.note: a regent rules on behalf of a monarch
to scan is to look over or check

explanation.surface: A surveyor uses a ruler to check a line on a map of a London waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent's Canal runs across north London; 'capital' means London. 'Using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This canal is a well-known waterway in London, the capital of England.

clue.text: Hole in crust here producing an eructation

definitions.text: Hole in crust here producing an eructation

parts.words: Hole in crust here producing an eructation
parts.note: the crust is the Earth's, and the belch is an eruption of lava from a vent

explanation.surface: A pie with a hole in its pastry gives someone indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crust' and 'eructation' (a belch) suggest food; they point to the Earth's crust and an eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain with a vent through the Earth's crust ejects lava and gas, a kind of geological belch.

clue.text: Lending money, game being unfinished on boat

indicators.note: on places the game after the boat in an across answer

parts.note: sub, short for submarine, is a boat

indicators.note: the word for the game is left without its last letter

parts.note: bingo is a numbers game

explanation.surface: Someone lends cash while an interrupted game is played on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being unfinished' cuts the last letter from BINGO, giving BING.
explanation.definitionFit: Subbing is informal British usage for lending someone money, giving them a sub or advance.

clue.text: Jog in one's birthday suit about midnight

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a birthday suit is bare skin, so this means naked
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A streaker goes jogging naked around midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like running; here it is a verb meaning a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a light push, such as a nudge with the elbow.

clue.text: Climb up here and join the party

definitions.text: Climb up here and join the party

parts.words: Climb up here and join the party
parts.note: a parade wagon carrying musicians, which joining a popular cause is likened to climbing aboard

explanation.surface: A host invites a guest to come up and join the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration; it is a political faction gaining popularity.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping on this wagon is an idiom for joining a popular movement or party.

clue.text: New wine goes to the head, producing repugnance

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: New wine goes straight to someone's head and makes them feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the head' suggests intoxication; it places the headland word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnance is the quality of being offensive or disgusting, as is nastiness.

clue.text: Quarrel to acquire lyrics

definitions.meaning: a verb: argue angrily with someone
literally, to come to possess the words of a song

explanation.surface: Two songwriters argue over who gets the lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for arguing literally says to possess words, the text of a song.

clue.text: Caustic words that could be thrown in your face

definitions.text: that could be thrown in your face
definitions.meaning: sulphuric acid, a corrosive liquid used in acid attacks

explanation.surface: Bitter insults are hurled at someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is both savage criticism and an old name for sulphuric acid, which can be thrown.

clue.text: Silver included in amount returned for sorcerer

indicators.note: included in places the metal inside the other piece
returned means the word for amount is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A sum of silver is handed back to a wizard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style 'returned' reading the amount runs backwards; Ag for silver comes from the Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a magician or sorcerer, like the Magi of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Real disaster headed off, dividing stretch of DNA

indicators.note: dividing says this piece splits the other in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a gene is a section of DNA

indicators.note: headed off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: ruin is a catastrophe or disaster

explanation.surface: A real disaster is averted, splitting a strand of DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headed off' looks like averting a disaster; here it beheads the word for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and real both mean authentic and not fake.

clue.text: Not in constant use, so last longer

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
wear is the damage from constant use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: A garment that is not used all the time lasts longer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to outlast it, remaining in use beyond it.

clue.text: Four at Henley somewhat eager

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rowing four at the Henley regatta are rather keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley hosts a famous rowing regatta on the Thames, where a four is a boat with four oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic or poetic adjective meaning early or eager.

clue.text: King's daughter at home to admirer joining the army

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is an admirer
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A princess at home with her admirer who has joined the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joining' is a link that adds the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of the king of Spain or Portugal.

clue.text: Clothes end in split

indicators.note: in places the goal inside the tear

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Clothes come to an end when they are torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like the end of the clothes; it means a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing.

clue.text: Alien with a collection of rare objects

parts.note: exotic means foreign, alien

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial owns a collection of curios.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or rare things from distant places, often collected.

clue.text: Beer talks hit trouble? Nonsense!

indicators.note: trouble stirs up and mixes the letters before it

explanation.surface: A drinker's chatter runs into difficulty, prompting a cry of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The print gives no letter count; the answer is twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatherskite is a Scottish word for foolish talk, or a person who talks it.
